problem: Dual-system and single-system VLN models built on VLMs suffer from a 2D-3D representation mismatch between generated 3D trajectories and VLM image features, monocular scale ambiguity, and large parameter counts (>=7B) or extra depth modules that block edge deployment.
motivation: VLMs have strong 2D semantics but lack metric 3D reasoning. Implicit latent alignment and added depth encoders raise latency and context length. An explicit, lightweight interface between geometry and the VLM, plus on-demand depth queries, could make small models accurate and deployable on-device.
key_idea: Treat a small VLM as the 'brain' that invokes perception and planning skills, choosing among 3D waypoints projected as pixel-aligned visual prompts and actively querying depth via a query-driven perceptual chain-of-thought.
insight: Explicit geometric interfaces and skill decomposition matter more than model size. In the incremental ablation on R2R-CE val-unseen, VLM-as-Brain with cross-space mapping lifts SR from 38.6 to 59.7, fine-grained self-correction (CDFG) adds to 65.6, and QD-PCoT adds to 67.2 SR with a small gain in NE. A history window of 8 frames is best; longer windows dilute attention.
method: VLM-as-Brain POSMDP: the VLM policy selects skills from a library, split into perception skills (tau=0, return augmented observations) and planning skills (tau>0, closed-loop execution with a termination condition beta).

Cross-space representation mapping: depth is back-projected into a global occupancy map, feasible 3D path waypoints are projected to the image plane via camera pose and intrinsics as pixel-aligned visual prompts, and the VLM picks one, which is restored to a 3D waypoint.

Context-driven fine-grained self-correction/active exploration: when no semantically relevant path projection is visible, the VLM outputs atomic Forward/Left/Right actions to look around and recover from deviations, then resumes skill invocation.

Query-Driven Perceptual CoT (QD-PCoT): under spatial ambiguity, the model issues a natural-language query (e.g. distance to an object), a perception skill returns geometric info, and after multi-round reasoning the model outputs target pixel coordinates that are back-projected with depth to a 3D goal.
Dynamic stage routing: navigation switches from global path navigation to local target localization when the target becomes visible.

AgentVLN-Instruct dataset: Habitat-based instruction-tuning data with target-visibility routing, skill invocation, injected trajectory noise with fine-grained fallbacks, and multi-round perceptual CoT; LLaVA-Video-178K is mixed in to preserve general ability.
Deployment: a 3B model runs locally on Jetson; the skill library uses RTAB-Map SLAM and path planners on a Unitree Go2 with a RealSense D455.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-3B (fine-tuned; visual encoder and projector frozen)
setting.training_data: AgentVLN-Instruct (Habitat-based, large-scale; size not given in main text) plus LLaVA-Video-178K
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB (640x480, 110° FOV) + depth + pose, 8-frame history
setting.action_space: skill calls (perception and planning skills that produce waypoints or target pixel coordinates) plus fine-grained Forward/Left/Right fallback actions
setting.privileged: none stated; depth and pose (odometry/SLAM) are used by the perception skills

results: AgentVLN-3B reaches 67.2 SR / 64.7 SPL on R2R-CE val-unseen, beating DualVLN-7.1B (64.3/58.5) and EfficientVLN-4B (64.2/55.9). On RxR-CE it gets 69.5 SR / 61.3 SPL / 74.6 nDTW, ahead of EfficientVLN-4B (67.0/54.3/68.4), while running on Jetson edge hardware.
limitations: Requires depth, pose, and SLAM/occupancy mapping (perception skills), so it is not purely monocular RGB; dependence on skill-library quality.
Real-world evaluation is only qualitative (no quantitative real-robot numbers in the main text), and simulator-only benchmarks are limited to R2R-CE and RxR-CE.
Dataset scale and construction details are deferred to the supplement; the ablation is on a single benchmark with no seed variance.
